findings.issue: The slot's enum (DataStandardEnum) permits only DICOM, BIDS, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, CDS, RO_CRATE, FHIR, OTHER. The top-level list is valid, but the value ordering aside, this is acceptable. However the same enum is used on every file_collections entry, where the value `CDS` is permitted and `ESDS`, `DICOM`, `OPEN_MHEALTH`, `WFDB`, `OMOP_CDM` are permitted — all values used conform. No defect confirmed here on enum membership; flagged only to record that each list was checked against the permitted set and all members are valid.

Organization object populated with `name` only and no `id`. Not a validation failure, but the AI-READI Consortium is the sole declared creator and the record elsewhere carries a ROR identifier (ROR:01yc7t268) for the accountable organization; the consortium itself has no identifier in the bundle, so omitting `id` is correct. No repair needed — recorded for completeness.

`source_caveats` is declared as a trust annotation about sibling slots, but this value also carries substantive dataset content ('The healthsheet states that the dataset was created by members of the AI-READI project, collectively referred to as the AI-READI Consortium, with member and institution details on the project website'). The affiliation-conflict portion is legitimate caveat material; the descriptive portion duplicates content that belongs in `notes` or is already carried by `affiliations`. Trim to the conflict statement only.

Grant `id` is `uriorcurie` and is populated with a NIH RePORTER resolver URL. The v5 rule directs that a `uriorcurie` slot take a CURIE where a prefix is declared; no NIH RePORTER prefix is declared in the schema digest, so a resolvable URL is the correct fallback. Acceptable as written. However the grant's award number OT2OD032644 — the actual identifier the bundle states — appears only in `notes`, not in the Grant object's own fields; the bundle supports it as the award number and it should be surfaced in the Grant `name` or an identifier field rather than buried in prose.

The NIH RePORTER record's award amount (5,026,499 USD) and project period (2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31) come from a tier-4 source and are correctly attributed, but the note conflates the original 2022 award record (application 10471118) with the later project-details link 10885481 used as the grant `id`. Both appear in the bundle; the note should state that two RePORTER records exist for the same core project number rather than presenting them as one continuous fact.

Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) is recorded as the accountable organization without caveat at this location, while `source_caveats` at the record root documents that the bundle does not reconcile Washington University in St. Louis (FAIRhub lead sponsor, managing organization, licensor, PI affiliation) against the University of Washington (RO-Crate PI department, IRB oversight, BMJ Open protocol). Both are tier-1/tier-2 sources. The unqualified value at this slot presents as settled what the record elsewhere says is unsettled. Add a `source_caveats` on the DataGovernance object pointing at the same conflict.

Set to `compliant`. The bundle supports that the public release was de-identified via the HIPAA Privacy Rule Safe Harbor method and that the team verified no HIPAA identifiers were present, but no source in the bundle makes a compliance determination in those terms. The enum value is an inference from the de-identification method. Either downgrade to omission or retain with a `source_caveats` recording that the value is derived from the stated Safe Harbor de-identification rather than from an explicit compliance statement.

Two SensitiveElement objects assert opposite values of `sensitive_elements_present` (false, then true) for the same dataset. Each carries a caveat noting the other, which is the correct handling of same-rank disagreement, but the record does not state which reading governs and a consumer reading only the boolean gets contradictory answers. The RO-Crate `rai:personalSensitiveInformation` list enumerates data-source categories (EHR, ECG, environmental sensor, CGM, accelerometer) rather than sensitive attributes in the schema's sense, which is likely why the two sources differ; that observation belongs in the caveat.

Omitted. The bundle states the dataset comprises tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data across DICOM, CSV, JSON and WFDB. No single B2AI_SUBSTRATE term covers a multimodal instance, so omission is correct per the digest's instruction to omit rather than approximate. Recorded to confirm the omission was deliberate.

Set to `false` on the ground that the healthsheet states the dataset does not identify demographic sub-populations, yet the same object's `distribution` field supplies aggregate counts by race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes status published in the dataset README. The boolean and the populated distribution are in tension: the README counts are dataset-level aggregates for the recommended split, not per-instance subpopulation labels, and the object should say so explicitly rather than leaving the reader to reconcile them.

The value opens with the FAIRhub de-identification type string 'NoDeIdentification', which in context means no active de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected. Presented at the head of the `method` field without that framing immediately adjacent, it reads as a claim that no de-identification was performed, which contradicts `identifiable_elements_present: false` and the Safe Harbor statement later in the same value. Reorder so the substantive method (Safe Harbor, no identifiers collected, verification performed) precedes the registry code.

States initial IRB approval received December 20, 2022. The bundle's healthsheet supports this date. However the record's `collection_timeframes` gives an actual study start of 2023-07-19 and the NIH award start as 2022-09-01; the approval date is consistent with both and no conflict exists. Recorded to confirm the date was checked rather than assumed.

`at_risk_groups_included: false` is an inference the bundle does not directly state. The IRB protocol's protected-populations checkboxes are unfilled in the retrieved form, and the record's own `source_caveats` says so. Deriving a positive `false` from unfilled checkboxes plus age and pregnancy exclusion criteria is reasonable but is reasoning, not evidence. The caveat is present and adequate; consider whether omitting the boolean and retaining only `special_protections` is the safer representation.

Eight VariableMetadata objects are supplied against a dataset whose clinical_data directory maps one-to-one to OMOP CDM tables and whose BMJ Open protocol tabulates roughly forty laboratory analytes with units and reference ranges. The selection is illustrative rather than complete, which is defensible, but nothing in the record says so. Add a note or caveat marking the list as a representative subset so a consumer does not read it as the full variable inventory.

HbA1c is given a unit but no reference range, while the BMJ Open protocol supplies 4.0–6.0 % for HbA1c. Several other variables in the record likewise omit ranges the bundle states. If reference ranges are to be carried at all, carry them consistently; note that a laboratory reference range is not the same as the variable's observed min/max and mapping it to `minimum_value`/`maximum_value` would misstate the field, so omission may be the correct choice — but it should be uniform.

356343 is stated as the dataset total, and the record's root `source_caveats` correctly notes that the nine datatype directories sum to 356,334 with the nine-file difference attributable to root-level metadata files. This is internally consistent and well documented. However the nine `file_collections` entries carry `file_count` values summing to 356,334 while the parent `total_file_count` is 356,343, and the slot description says the total 'can be aggregated from file_collections[].file_count'. The discrepancy is explained in the root caveat but not at either numeric slot; a reader checking the arithmetic at `total_file_count` finds no explanation there.

3815969779678 is taken from the FAIRhub API `data.size`. The nine file_collections `total_bytes` values sum to 3,815,974,377,264, which exceeds the declared total by roughly 4.6 GB. Neither the bundle nor the record explains the difference. Either the per-directory sizes and the dataset total come from different snapshots, or the total excludes something the directories include. Add a caveat recording the arithmetic mismatch.

Omitted. The bundle supplies `contentUrl: https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3` in the RO-Crate and an access URL `https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access`, and the FAIRhub page carries an 'Access this dataset' action. The DOI resolver is not a direct data URL and the access page is a gated workflow rather than a download, so omission is defensible under the slot's 'points directly to the data itself' wording. Recorded to confirm the omission was reasoned; the access route is already carried in `data_governance.access_review_process`.

Four DistributionFormat objects are given with `format`, `media_type` and `notes`, but none carries `access_urls` or `download_url` despite the bundle supplying the FAIRhub dataset URL and the access-conditions URL. More importantly the four media types are the dataset's internal file formats (from the FAIRhub `format` array), not distribution packaging. The slot asks how the dataset is made available; the bundle states access is via the FAIRhub platform with verified-ID login, and that a smaller mini-subset is available for pipeline development. That distribution information is absent from this slot and appears only in `data_governance` and `version_access`.
Omitted. Nothing in the bundle states a compression format for the release. Correct omission.

Omitted, while `use_repository[0].repository_details` records that the healthsheet states the dataset had not been used for any tasks at the time of writing. That negative statement is evidence about existing uses and is currently carried in the wrong slot: `use_repository` is for repositories tracking use, and the 'no known uses' fact is padding it out. Either add an ExistingUse recording the negative, or drop the statement — but per the v2 rule a value recording that something is absent has not answered the field, so omission of `existing_uses` is likely correct and the sentence should be trimmed from `use_repository`.

Mixes three distinct facts: FAIRhub usage statistics (views 24,636, citations 0), the healthsheet's statement that no repository links papers using the dataset, and the citation requirement. The middle statement contradicts the object's own existence — the object asserts a use-tracking repository while its text says none exists. FAIRhub's usage dashboard is a legitimate use-tracking resource, so the object should stand on that alone; the 'no repository' statement should be removed or moved.

Omitted while `prohibited_uses` carries six entries. The bundle's healthsheet answers the discouraged-use question by pointing at the licence restrictions, which are already captured under `prohibited_uses`. Omission is therefore defensible and avoids duplicating the same licence terms across two slots. Recorded to confirm the split between prohibited and discouraged was deliberate.

Omitted. The bundle supports that the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and intended to support applications beyond those originally planned — the healthsheet describes it as 'aimed at facilitating multiple potential downstream AI/ML applications' and the licence permits commercial and non-commercial derivative work. This is weaker than the material already in `tasks` and `intended_uses`, and omission avoids restating them. Acceptable.
Both omitted, consistent with `labeling_strategies` recording that no labels are provided and no annotation was performed. Correct omissions.

Omitted. The bundle states under cleaning that missing data 'that can be directly filled from other portions of an individual's record' were filled during quality control. That is a form of deterministic imputation and is currently recorded only inside `cleaning_strategies` and `missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy`. Whether it rises to an ImputationProtocol is a judgment call; if retained as-is, no change needed, but the overlap across three slots should be reduced.

Omitted while the bundle clearly describes a public release and a controlled-access release containing additional variables (5-digit zip code, sex, race, ethnicity, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications, traffic and accident reports), and additionally a mini-subset for pipeline development. These are logical partitions of the dataset that the bundle supports as DataSubset entries. The controlled-access distinction is currently described in five separate prose fields (`description`, `data_governance`, `participant_privacy`, `known_limitations`, `is_deidentified`) rather than represented structurally.

Both omitted. The RO-Crate declares nine subcrates via `hasPart`, which are represented as `file_collections` rather than as `resources`. Given the slot description directs file groupings to `file_collections`, this is the correct choice. Correct omission.

Both use `doi:` CURIEs to point at journal articles rather than datasets. `DatasetRelationship.target_dataset` is required and the relationship type `is_described_by` is a permitted enum member, so this validates, but the slot names a dataset and the targets are publications. The bundle supports both publications as associated works; if the schema offers no publication-relationship slot, `external_resources` would carry them more honestly. At minimum the mismatch should be noted.

Version 1.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.1) is described in `version_access.versions_available` but has no DatasetRelationship entry, while version 2.0.0 does. The bundle supports both prior versions equally. Either add an `is_new_version_of` entry for 1.0.0 or state why only the immediately preceding version is linked.

Omitted. The healthsheet's erratum question was returned with an empty response in the bundle, so there is no evidence of any erratum. Correct omission — an empty source answer is not evidence of absence but also supports no value.

Omitted. The bundle states that recruitment pools were identified by screening electronic health records at the three sites, and `raw_data_sources` records those EHR systems. However the dataset instances are prospectively collected rather than derived from the EHR content, so the EHR is a recruitment source rather than a derivation source. Omission is correct.

All omitted. The bundle supplies `created_at: 1763366400` (2025-11-17) in the FAIRhub API and `datePublished: 11/17/25` in the RO-Crate, both of which are the publication date already carried in `issued`. No separate creation or modification timestamp for the record or the dataset is stated. Correct omissions.

Correctly records the 2023-07-19 versus 18 July 2023 disagreement and the preference. However `timeframe_details` also states 'Approximately 4 percent of participants are expected to undergo a follow-up examination in year 4' while the NIH RePORTER abstract and the FAIRhub study description both say 10 percent, and the BMJ Open protocol says 4 percent. That is a second unrecorded disagreement between a tier-4/tier-1 source (10%) and a tier-3 source (4%); the higher-ranked value of 10% should govern, or both should be recorded.

States collection 'between July 19, 2023 and May 1, 2025' and '2,280 adults'. Both are supported. The description also asserts the dataset is 'harmonized across three data collection sites' and names them; supported. However it states the release 'contains 356,343 files totalling approximately 3.82 TB' without the caveat that the per-directory figures do not sum to either total. Cross-reference the root `source_caveats` from the description or accept the root caveat as sufficient.

Set to `false`. The dataset contains substantial tabular content (OMOP CDM CSVs, participants.tsv, manifest.tsv) alongside imaging and waveform data, so it is not purely tabular; `false` is the correct answer for a mixed-modality dataset under the slot's 'True if the data is structured as a table' wording. Correct.

Three purposes, three gaps and three tasks are recorded, and several restate one another in different words — the salutogenesis objective appears in `purposes[0]`, `purposes[1]`, `tasks[1]` and `addressing_gaps[1]`. Each slot's framing differs enough to justify separate entries, but the overlap is heavy and the temporal-atlas language is near-verbatim across `purposes[1]` and `tasks[1]`. Tighten so each slot carries what only it carries.

Nine keywords drawn from the FAIRhub subject list and the study keyword list. 'Retinal imaging' appears once here but the FAIRhub source lists it twice with differing capitalization ('Retinal Imaging' in the RO-Crate, 'Retinal imaging' in the subject array); the single normalized entry is correct. No defect.

Carries two facts: device-manufacturer loans/discounts, and the 'repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' notice. The second is a statement about the hosting platform's status, not about the dataset's content, and is genuinely residual. The first — that manufacturers loaned devices at no cost and gave research discounts — is a funding/contribution fact that `funders` could carry as an in-kind contribution. Consider moving.

Populated with the string 'AI-READI custom license v2.0', matching the FAIRhub `rights.rightsName`. The FAIRhub pages elsewhere label it 'Health Data License' and the RO-Crate gives `license: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036`. The record carries the Zenodo DOI and the 'Health Data License' label inside `license_and_use_terms.license_terms` prose but the scalar `license` slot carries only one of three attested forms without a caveat. Add a caveat, or prefer the tier-1 FAIRhub `rightsName` explicitly and say so.

The second sentence ('The healthsheet reports no additional third-party intellectual property restrictions beyond those in the license') is a statement that something is absent. Per the v2 rule, a value recording that information is absent has not answered the field. The first sentence answers it; trim the second.

Records that the RO-Crate's `confidentialityLevel` of 'HL7:2N (normal)' does not map onto the schema's `confidentiality_level` enum (unrestricted/restricted/confidential) and is therefore carried in prose. This is the right handling. However `confidentiality_level` is then left unpopulated entirely, when the bundle's access model — verified-ID login, use-restriction attestation, licence agreement — supports `restricted` for the public release. Consider populating the enum from the access model with a caveat, or state why no enum value was chosen.

All omitted. The bundle names a Data Access Committee in the BMJ Open protocol but gives no membership, contact, appeal route or decision timeframe, stating only that controlled-access requirements were under development. Correct omissions.

Combines the public self-attestation flow with the controlled-access data use agreement and the BMJ Open note that requirements were still being developed. The BMJ Open statement is tier-3 and dates from the protocol paper; the tier-1 FAIRhub `accessType: PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired` and `accessDetails` describe the current v3.0.0 flow. Presenting a superseded 'under development' status alongside the current flow without dating it risks reading as current. Attribute the developmental statement to the protocol paper explicitly.
Correctly set to the bridge2ai data-sheets-schema URI and `Dataset` respectively, and correctly distinguished from `conforms_to`, which carries the dataset's own content standards. No defect.

All nine use fragments on the dataset DOI (e.g. `doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#cardiac_ecg`). Per the v5/v6 rules this is the correct minting pattern for a part of this dataset. However no other value in the record points at any of these fragments — no split, task, distribution or subset cites them. Under the v6 rule, a part that nothing points at should be described rather than labelled, so these identifiers are noise that reads as structure. Either add the pointers that would justify them or accept that `id` is required on FileCollection and the fragments are the least-bad way to satisfy it.

All nine are set to `processed_data`. This is accurate — every directory holds standardized, converted output rather than device-native raw files, and the record states raw data are retained but not shared. Correct and consistent.

clinical_data is given 7 files at 176,182,781 bytes. The bundle's structure description supports both figures. However the same directory is described as containing 'each CSV file ... a one-to-one mapping to the OMOP CDM tables' plus a dqd_omop.json — seven files is a small number for an OMOP CDM instance covering 2,280 participants across many domains. The figure is what the source states and should stand, but its terseness relative to the description invites a caveat.

Each collection carries both a prose `conforms_to` naming the standards and a `conforms_to_standard` enum list. This is the pattern the digest asks for — prose in the source's words, enum for queryability — and the two agree in every case. Correct.

Omitted while the other three booleans are set. The bundle does not state that any data were inferred or derived from other data — the healthsheet answer covers directly observable and subject-reported only — so omission rather than `false` is defensible, but the asymmetry with three populated siblings reads as an oversight rather than a decision. Either set `false` or note the omission.
Twelve CollectionMechanism objects, each one distinct instrument or instrument family, correctly not collapsed. Consistent with the v2 one-object-per-entity rule. No defect.

Set to `false` with `strategies` explaining that 'The dataset itself contains all participants enrolled within the collection window rather than a sample of them', matching the healthsheet's 'The dataset contains all possible instances'. But `why_not_representative` is populated, and that field presupposes the dataset is a sample of some larger set. The object simultaneously denies being a sample and explains why the sample is unrepresentative. Resolve: the cohort is a non-probability sample of the study base (all patients aged 40+ with an encounter at the three sites), and `source_data` already says so — so `is_sample: true` with the healthsheet's 'all enrolled participants' framing moved to `strategies` is the coherent reading.

Omitted while `is_representative: false` is asserted. The healthsheet states representativeness was not validated; recording that explicitly would answer the field. Currently the reader cannot tell whether verification was attempted and failed or never attempted.

All nine entries populate the required `source_description`; several also carry `raw_data_format` or `source_type` or `access_details`. Population is uneven — the EHR entry has `source_type` but no format, the format-only entries have no `source_type` — but each field is populated where the bundle supports it. Acceptable.

The watermarking entry describes a distribution-security control, not a preprocessing step applied to the data in preparation for analysis. It duplicates material already in `regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions` and `participant_privacy.privacy_techniques`. Remove from `preprocessing_strategies`.

Contains the audit statement ('has not undergone any formal external audits, but has been reviewed internally by AI-READI team members'). Audit history is not a cleaning procedure; it belongs in `notes` or, as a trust annotation, in `source_caveats`. The dqd_omop.json data-quality-dashboard fact is legitimately a cleaning/QC artefact and should stay.

The single object records that no labeling was performed and enumerates the sub-questions that consequently have no answer. Per the v2 rule, a value stating that information is absent has not answered the field. The substantive fact — that the dataset is deliberately hypothesis-agnostic and ships without labels — is real and worth recording, but it belongs in `description` or `notes`; `labeling_strategies` should be omitted.

Omitted while the bundle lists precisely what was removed from the public release: HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers, sex, race/ethnicity, and medications. That enumeration currently sits in `deidentification_details` prose. Populate the dedicated field.

Carries both the substantive description (written, electronic or in-person) and the FAIRhub registry code 'ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised'. Both are attested and the ordering puts the substantive content first. Acceptable.

Given as the string '200 US dollars'. The bundle's healthsheet says '$200 for the study visit' and the IRB protocol says 'a $200 stipend'. Consistent. However the IRB protocol also states 'The amount may be changed in future years depending on the study funding', which is material to anyone reading the figure as fixed and is not recorded.

'AI-READI ethics team' is not an organization the bundle names as such; the RO-Crate lists four individuals under `ethicalReview`. Coining a body name for a list of people is a mild fabrication of structure. Either use `contact_person` for one of the named individuals and describe the group in `review_details`, or rename to reflect what the source says.

Bundles the four named ethics reviewers, the general ELSI commitment, the bioethicist guidance, and the Native Biodata Consortium engagement into one value. The Native Biodata Consortium engagement concerns American Indian and Alaska Native data governance and is a distinct activity from the internal ethics review; it warrants its own entry or a move to `notes`.

Gives all three version dates in one string. The slot is singular-valued within a multivalued DistributionDate list; three distinct release events would more naturally be three objects. Not a validation failure but collapses three entities into one per the v2 rule.
`doi:10.60775/fairhub.3` as a `uriorcurie` with a declared `doi:` prefix. Correct form per the v5 rule.
A single string enumerating all three versions with their DOIs, dates, participant counts and sizes. The field is a list; three versions should be three entries.
'Approximately once a year', matching the healthsheet and RO-Crate `rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan`. Correct.

Omitted on both entries. The bundle states the dataset is self-contained and relies on documentation only for provenance context, and that the documentation is CC-BY 4.0. Nothing states whether the documentation is archived, so omission is correct — but `future_guarantees` on entry [0] is populated with a statement about the dataset's self-containment rather than about guarantees that the external resource will persist, which is what the field asks. Move that sentence.

`content_warnings_present: false` with a note restating the healthsheet's negative answer. A ContentWarning object whose entire content is 'there are no content warnings' populates the slot without warning of anything. Per the v2 rule this is a value recording absence; omit the slot.

Same pattern as content_warnings: `confidential_elements_present: false` plus a restatement of the negative. Consider omitting, though the explicit 'no personally identifiable information is included' does carry information a reader of a health dataset would want affirmed, so retention is defensible here in a way it is not for content_warnings.
The single object's entire content is 'No data protection impact analysis has been conducted for the dataset.' This is a value recording that something does not exist. Omit the slot.
States that no mechanism exists for outside contribution. Same absence-recording pattern; omit the slot.

'There are no limits on the retention of the data' is a substantive policy statement rather than a bare absence — a reader learns that data will not be deleted on a schedule. Retention is justified here.

Omitted, correctly, since the raw data are explicitly not shared. But the RawData object's entire content is that the raw data exist and are not shared — again an absence-shaped value. It carries the forward-looking fact that raw data may appear in future controlled-access releases, which is substantive; retain on that basis.

Five DataAnomaly objects, each a distinct failure mode, correctly not collapsed. The fifth mixes three device-specific quality issues (Optomed handheld variability, Spectralis operator dependence, FLIO compliance) that could be three entries. Minor.
Populated with a single string naming both race/ethnicity groups and diabetes severity groups. The field is a list; two distinct subset families should be two entries.
All four values (selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias) are members of the declared BiasTypeEnum. Correct.

All five values (representativeness_limitation, coverage_limitation, scope_limitation ×2, temporal_limitation) are members of the declared enum. Two entries share `scope_limitation` for genuinely distinct limitations (release-scope omissions; eligibility restrictions), which is permitted. Correct.

Carries the full split rationale, proportions, counts and per-split age statistics in one prose block, and duplicates the aggregate counts already in `subpopulations[0].distribution`. The overlap between the two slots should be reduced; `splits` should keep the split-specific figures and `subpopulations` the cohort-level ones.
`B2AI_TOPIC:43` (Diabetes). Correct CURIE form against the declared vocabulary and an apt single term for a dataset whose organizing condition is type 2 diabetes.
`false`, consistent with `labeling_strategies` and the healthsheet's repeated 'no labels are provided'. Correct.

Omitted while `missing_data_documentation` at the top level carries the same material. The Instance-level field would carry per-instance missingness; the bundle's statement that 'not all modalities are available for all participants' is exactly per-instance missingness. Duplication risk either way; current placement at the top level is acceptable.

States 'approximately 4 to 10 percent of participants are expected to be invited for a follow-up examination in year 4', hedging across the same 4%/10% source disagreement flagged at `collection_timeframes`. Presenting a range where the sources give two discrete figures obscures the conflict rather than recording it. State the higher-ranked figure and caveat the other.

The root caveat is thorough and correctly records seven disagreements with rankings and preferences. Two further disagreements identified in this audit are not covered: the 4% versus 10% longitudinal follow-up fraction, and the licence-name variants ('AI-READI custom license v2.0' / 'Health Data License' / the Zenodo DOI). Add both.

Gives the FAIRhub dataset citation from the RO-Crate `associatedPublication`. The bundle also states, in the licence and the healthsheet and both FAIRhub pages, that users must follow the citation instructions at docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/citation rather than a fixed string. The fixed citation is attested in the RO-Crate so it stands, but the instruction-based requirement is the operative one and is recorded nowhere in the record.

summary: Audited the full record against the declared bundle. No fabricated facts were found: every substantive value traces to the bundle, identifiers use declared prefixes correctly (doi:, ORCID:, ROR:, B2AI_TOPIC:), all enum values are members of their declared enums, and the root source_caveats block handles seven genuine source disagreements with explicit ranking justification. Principal defects fall into five groups. (1) Absence-recording values: content_warnings, data_protection_impacts, extension_mechanism and labeling_strategies each consist solely of a statement that something does not exist, which under the v2 rule has not answered the field; these should be omitted, with their substantive residue moved to notes or description. (2) Arithmetic inconsistencies left unexplained at the point of use: file_collections file_counts sum to 356,334 against a stated total of 356,343 (explained only in the root caveat) and total_bytes sum to roughly 4.6 GB more than the stated total_size_bytes (unexplained anywhere). (3) Unrecorded source disagreements: the 4% versus 10% longitudinal follow-up fraction appears hedged as a range in relationships and stated as 4% in collection_timeframes without caveat, and the licence carries three attested names with only one in the scalar license slot. (4) Slot-fit and collapsing problems: distribution_formats carries internal file formats rather than distribution channels; watermarking sits in preprocessing_strategies; audit history sits in cleaning_strategies; distribution_dates and version_access.versions_available each collapse three release events into one string; sampling_strategies simultaneously asserts is_sample false and populates why_not_representative. (5) Structural under-representation: the public versus controlled-access split is described across five prose fields but has no DataSubset entries, and the nine file_collections fragment identifiers are pointed at by nothing in the record. Two governance items warrant attention beyond mechanics: the Washington University in St. Louis versus University of Washington institutional conflict is caveated at the root but presented unqualified at data_governance.accountable_organization, and the two contradictory sensitive_elements booleans, while each correctly caveated as same-rank disagreement, leave a consumer reading only the booleans with opposite answers.
